newsitem.title: USA: California utilities called to unbundle metering.
newsitem.headline: California utilities called to unbundle metering.

text.p: A California Public Utilities Commission (CPUC) administrative law judge (ALJ) has called for investor-owned utilities to "unbundle" the cost of distribution services as the electric industry deregulates.
The draft decision issued this week must still be accepted by the five-member CPUC, which is expected to address the issue at a regular meeting on March 18.

Unbundling of services including metering and billing is opposed by the state's largest utilities, Edison International's Southern California Edison Co and PG&E Corp's Pacific Gas and Electric Co, which would prefer to retain the existing monopoly system.
But the ALJ opinion concluded that "competing energy service providers should be allowed to present consolidated bills that reflect the full cost of electricity" and to provide their own meters.
Under legislation passed last year, a cross-section of California consumers will be able to choose their electricity supplier starting next January.
